html:
The January Uprising was a Polish and Lithuanian rising against the Russian Empire that began on 22 January 1863, set off by a forced draft of young men into the Russian army, and lasted into 1864.

It was a guerrilla war of small partisan bands against a large army, run by a secret national government in Warsaw. It spread to Lithuania and parts of Belarus. The rebels promised land to peasants, but Russia offered the peasants better terms and won many over. Tens of thousands were killed in battle or executed, and some tens of thousands were sent to Siberia. Russia then banned Polish in schools and offices and abolished what was left of the Kingdom of Poland's autonomy. After it Poles turned to organic work, building schools and businesses, until the rebirth of the Polish state in 1918. It followed the November Uprising.
